Quasiplanar Fusionist.name: Quasiplanar Fusionist
Quasiplanar Fusionist.text:
To some, mastery of the arcane is not enough. Some of the greatest minds in wizardry have dedicated their lives to harnessing other traditions of magic the way they can with arcana. Over the centuries, many have failed, but recent breakthroughs in planar fusion have led to the discovery of a force known as quasiplanar fluxes.

Fluxes are echoes of planar energy from other realms that when calibrated properly, can be used to channel spells of other traditions. The fluxes can take on many forms; a spark of limitless primal magic on one’s fingertip, a halo of divine power, a strange stream of occult energy shrouding one’s eyes, or it might be nearly invisible, appearing as complex diagrams taking up whole chapters of a wizard’s spellbook as the author tries to interpolate energy extraction into a schema.

To choose Quasiplanar Fusionist, simply choose @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-player-options.n0f3V2gE9U6wmdQd]{School of Quasiplanar Fusionism} as your arcane school.

New Class Feats.name: New Class Feats
New Class Feats.text:
NEW TRAITS

Exploit With enough study, a wizard can learn to take advantage of the loopholes and rule gaps of magic to reconstitute its power into another form. This gives the wizard unique and unusual ways to make arcane magic obey them through subverting a spell’s normal behavior by either compressing it into a reactive rebuttal or unraveling it carefully to produce an alternate effect. Using an exploit costs a prepared arcane spell slot with specific qualities and the rank of the spell slot you expend determines the strength of the effects. You can use only one action with the exploit trait per round. For the purposes of counteract checks, exploits are treated as spells equal to the rank of the expended spell.

Experimental Changes

Second Thesis

This experimental change is listed for those that believe thesis with particularly strong scaling over other theses end up prioritized over more thematic choices. This is a power increase to wizards that are at least 11th level, but not a substantial increase when comparing the most powerful thesis choices.

Intro.name: Intro
Intro.text:
Foreward

There may not be a more disputed class within Pathfinder itself. The wizard’s tenured connection to magic, long-standing history in table-top systems, and the sheer amount of conceptual ground form a unique triumvirate. Can one even reduce a wizard to a single concept? Long robes and a pointy hat come to mind, sure, but over the years a wizard has grown to encompass many types of learned magic. Whether they wield fire, staves, the dead, or trickery as their weapons of choice, the name ‘wizard’ describes one who has tamed magic through logic and tact. Even with this common thread, the answers to what a wizard should or should not be are as varied as its umbrella of concepts. Through the course of writing this book and testing its contents, there were many discussions, sometimes even battles, to find the heart of the answer. And although the task to define a wizard may never be truly accomplished, we can say that we feel that we gave it effort+. May this help you be a mighty wizard, whatever that may mean to you.

Wizards+

Turning the ordinary into the extraordinary is the life of a wizard. A simple piece of paper and words begets an earthshaking power beyond measure. Wizards do not merely wield magic through whim, as each spell is a carefully architected piece with a grand purpose. No, they wield it with pragmatism, cunning, and sometimes even mischief. Each wizard harnesses not only creativity, but a responsibility to magic, illuminating its possibilities and confronting the shadows of its consequences. Whether they choose to challenge the status quo, or merely they seek to learn what magic has to offer, they proceed with reason as their companion for the journey.

New Arcane Schools.name: New Arcane Schools
New Arcane Schools.text:
A lesson learned is a lesson earned, as they say, and wizards do their fair share of the learning from their arcane schools. A wizard may be self-taught and merely a follower of an arcane school, but whatever their alma mater, the learning does not end until the wizard walks the roads to the Boneyard.
